sources.entry: SoundLadder - Menu bar app that picks the audio output from a ranked list and falls back to the next connected device automatically. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/dirkkredinger/SoundLadder) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: SoundLadder is a small macOS menu bar app that picks the audio output from a user-ranked device list and falls back to the next connected device automatically.
summary.what_it_does: SoundLadder lets you drag and drop all detected macOS output devices into a preferred order. When devices connect or disconnect, including Bluetooth devices, it switches the default output to the highest-ranked device that is currently available. Disconnected devices keep their place in the list. You can exclude devices such as virtual ones from automatic selection, optionally route system sounds too, and switch manually from the menu bar icon. The app offers English and German interfaces and states it has no tracking, no network access and no dependencies beyond Apple frameworks.
use_cases: keep headphones as the default audio output when they reconnect
fall back to built-in speakers when a USB headset is unplugged
stop macOS from switching sound to the last connected device
exclude virtual audio devices from automatic switching
quick switch audio output from the menu bar
notable: Ranked priority list with drag and drop ordering of output devices
Remembers disconnected devices so they keep their place in the ladder
No tracking, no network access, no third-party dependencies
Optional routing of system sounds such as alerts and effects
caveats: Not notarized by Apple, so macOS blocks the first launch and the user must allow it under Privacy & Security
Homebrew 7+ requires trusting the third-party tap before installing
